reason: While the text does depict the conflict at a national level (Hebrew people vs. Egyptian people) and emphasizes collective action rather than personal disputes, it is fundamentally inaccurate to claim the conflict is NOT religious. The entire narrative is saturated with religious elements: God repeatedly identifies Himself as 'the God of the Hebrews' (יְהוָה אֱלֹהֵ֣י הָֽעִבְרִ֔ים), the core issue is the Israelites' freedom to worship ('Let My people go that they may serve Me'), the Ten Plagues are divinely initiated punishments, and God's supernatural deliverance through the Red Sea is the climactic moment. The conflict is presented as God's battle against Pharaoh and Egypt. Though the statement correctly identifies a national dimension, it fundamentally mischaracterizes the religious dimension as absent when it is actually central to the entire narrative framework.
